On 2012-Feb-23, at 08:34 , Atanas Koulov wrote:
>
> Thanks a lot! I am still struggling with the NAs that cut produces...

Cut produces NAs when the data is outside of the range of the breaks, so you should alter your breaks accordingly. For example:

cut(hwy, breaks=c(-Inf, 10,15,20,30, Inf))

shouldn't produce any NA.

> [97] (20,30] (20,30] (15,20] (30, Inf] (30, Inf] (30, Inf] (20,30] (30, Inf] (30, Inf] (30, Inf] (30, Inf] (20,30]

This is what I told you above: you need to " create a new column in the dataset with the cut version of hwy"

library("ggplot2")

# for information
head(mpg)

# cut hwy in factor levels
range(mpg$hwy)
mpg$hwyF <- cut(mpg$hwy, breaks=c(10, 15, 20, 30, 50))
class(mpg$hwyF)

qplot(x=hwyF, fill=class, data=mpg, geom="histogram")
# or
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=hwyF, fill=class), data=mpg)
